name: Neurenteric cyst

criteria.description: Identification of a well-defined cystic lesion adjacent to the spinal cord or brainstem on MRI or CT
Histopathological confirmation showing cyst lined by columnar or cuboidal epithelium of endodermal origin
Presence of neurological symptoms consistent with cyst location such as myelopathy or radiculopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic lesion on imaging plus histopathological confirmation of endodermal epithelial lining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical biopsy for definitive confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intramedullary cystic lesion causing spinal cord compression
Cyst lined by endodermal-derived epithelium on histology
searchTerms: cyst with specific tissue lining on biopsy

common.symptomName: Radicular pain corresponding to cyst location
searchTerms: nerve root pain at cyst location

common.symptomName: Sensory disturbances including numbness or paresthesia
Neck or back pain localized to cyst site

occasional.symptomName: Bladder or bowel dysfunction due to spinal cord involvement
Headache related to intracranial cyst location
Cranial nerve palsies in brainstem cysts
searchTerms: facial muscle weakness from brainstem cyst
fluid buildup in brain from cyst blockage
brain swelling secondary to cyst obstruction

rare.symptomName: Spinal deformities such as scoliosis associated with cyst
Spontaneous cyst rupture causing acute neurological deterioration
searchTerms: sudden cyst rupture causing neurological decline
rapid neurological deterioration after cyst breaks

imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed cystic lesion adjacent to spinal cord or brainstem
CT may show cyst with fluid density without enhancement
other: Histopathology demonstrating cyst lined by columnar or cuboidal endodermal epithelium
Presence of mucinous or proteinaceous cyst contents

distinguishingFeatures: Arachnoid cysts are lined by arachnoid membrane, not endodermal epithelium
Typically do not contain mucinous material
Usually located in subarachnoid space rather than intramedullary
Epidermoid cysts contain keratin debris and are lined by squamous epithelium
Do not have endodermal epithelial lining

redFlags: Signs of spinal cord compression such as paralysis or severe sensory loss
Acute neurological deterioration suggesting cyst rupture or hemorrhage
references: Wilkins RH, Rengachary SS. Neurosurgery. 2nd ed. McGraw-Hill; 1996.
Kumar R, et al. Neurenteric cysts of the spine: a review. Neurosurg Focus. 2011;30(3):E10.
